claims.text: The proposed computational method uses density functional theory with phonon-dispersion calculations.
The proposed method can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The method is applied to initially untested high-entropy alloys.
Phonon dispersion and lattice dynamics are the structural mediator used by the predictive approach.
Ab initio calculations or molecular-dynamics simulations can predict phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed approach will improve predictive accuracy relative to existing methods.
The proposed approach could yield phonon thermal-conductivity values 10–20% lower than current predictions.
The approach is limited to high-entropy alloys considered for thermal-insulation applications.
Scalability and computational-resource requirements may limit the approach.
The approach may not have uniform accuracy across different high-entropy alloys and operating conditions.
The benchmark will compare predictions from the proposed method and current methods against experimental phonon thermal-conductivity measurements for a set of high-entropy alloys.
Phonon thermal conductivity will be measured using time-domain thermoreflectance or laser-induced transient grating.
The hypothesis is falsified if the new method fails to improve accuracy by more than 5% over current predictions.
The hypothesis is falsified if predicted phonon thermal-conductivity values do not correlate with experimental measurements.
